set.body:
Objective:
Prove that the Frame foundation is coherent, cross-platform, independently buildable, and ready to extract from the ScalaFIM repository without package or dependency surgery.

Acceptance gate:
- frame-core and the local engine import no ScalaFIM or Gale packages and have no build dependency on internal ScalaFIM modules.
- Package and artifact identities are neutral and documented as an explicit exception to the temporary host repository convention.
- JVM and Scala.js compile and test gates cover storage, ownership, dynamic and typed APIs, relational semantics, optimizer laws, local execution, and baseline IO.
- Compile-negative tests prove field lookup, operator typing, join collisions, and nullability propagation.
- Arrow-layout fixtures and interop roundtrips verify physical fidelity without treating Parquet decoding or matrix packing as zero-copy.
- Resource tests and allocator diagnostics show that batch streams, retained slices, failed actions, and early termination close correctly.
- Runnable examples cover inspect dynamic data, clean it, promote to a named-tuple schema, filter, group, join, explain, collect, and write.
- Bench receipts report scan, filter/project fusion, grouped aggregation, join, UTF-8, slicing, allocation, and JVM/JS profiles with explicit hardware/runtime metadata.
- A standalone build or extraction rehearsal compiles the Frame modules outside the ScalaFIM aggregate.
- README and architecture docs state what Frame owns, what adapters own, and what remains out of scope.

Out of foundation scope:
DuckDB, Parquet pushdown, Gale vectors/matrices, ScalaFIM neuroimaging features, Spark, hybrid plan segmentation, spill, statistical models, and formula/design-matrix construction.
set.title: Frame foundation 6: cross-platform laws, evidence, documentation, and extraction gate
